coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a one-off full crawl of stikk.org/en/members/*, classify each member by whether it names financial-services clients, and promote the banking-relevant subset to individually tracked sources.

coverage_gaps.description: ATM/self-service hardware OEMs (NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf) and PIN-pad/POS OEMs (Verifone, Ingenico, PAX) were not individually searched for Kosovo partners or press releases.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add an ARBK entity lookup step for every vendor name in the actor map; registered-director changes are a legally-filed leadership-move signal that bypasses corporate PR entirely.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define a compliant analyst workflow (manual review or licensed data) for a watchlist of vendor company pages and Kosovo-based employee profiles, rather than attempting automated collection.

brief: Kosovo's banking-technology supplier layer is genuinely observable even though the banks themselves are private and disclose almost nothing: the productive sources are the vendors' own channels, not the banks'. The strongest confirmed nodes are Quipu (ProCredit's captive IT arm, with a Prishtina card-personalisation centre serving 25+ institutions and steady local implementation-engineer hiring), Mellon Kosova (ATM/EFT-POS field service, est. 2013 Prishtina), Printec's Kosovo entity, ASEE/Payten's reported market-share build in Kosovo, Halcom's e-banking footprint, and local integrators such as IPKO — whose PriBank critical-banking-infrastructure partnership was announced in Albanian media rather than by the bank. Hiring ads on KosovaJob and pointer aggregators (STIKK member directory, Kosovo Banking Association events and committee elections, vendor partner locators) are the highest-yield recurring feeds, while classic core-banking vendor case studies naming Kosovo banks appear not to exist publicly. The main open weaknesses are LinkedIn (where country-manager moves almost certainly live but collection is ToS-constrained), the unqueried ARBK company registry for registered-director changes, and unenumerated ATM/POS OEM partner networks.
